result.headline: The CNN reached a test mean of 13.25 apples (seed mean 12.36, spread 0.78), less than half the MLP's 31.6 to 31.9 on the same full-board view, and its learning curve was still climbing when the 10 minutes ran out.
result.summary: The CNN (convolutional network: small filters that scan the board for local patterns) played 100 fixed test games with a mean of 13.25 apples, a median of 13, and a best game of 31. Its three seeds gave 11.76, 12.08 and 13.25. Every test game ended in a body crash except one wall crash, with 96 steps per game and 7 steps per apple. The MLP (fully connected network) on the same view scored 31.87 and 31.64, with 273 steps per game. The CNN ran at roughly 170 env steps per second, against roughly 1,000 for the MLP, so it took about 103,000 steps in 10 minutes while the MLP took about 650,000. Its training curve stayed flat near 0.1 to 0.3 apples for the first 3 minutes, then rose steeply: mean_last_100 went from 1.08 at 4.6 minutes to 10.36 at 10 minutes. Training still reflects some exploration, so the test score is the number to trust.
result.diagnosis: The most likely cause is that the CNN is undertrained, not that a CNN is a poor fit for this board. It spent its first few minutes slowly learning while the MLP was already much further along, and each step costs about six times more compute. Exploration also decays over 100,000 steps (eps_decay_steps), and the CNN only reached about 103,000 steps, so it likely explored heavily for almost the whole run. The learned behaviour is efficient about finding apples (7 steps per apple, close to the MLP's 9) but it runs into its own body after a short life. That points to a snake that has not yet learned to keep its body clear as it grows. Two seeds of the same recipe agree closely, so the gap to the MLP is real for this budget, though one 10-minute run per seed cannot show what 30 minutes would give.
result.learned: A network built for pictures is not automatically better: with a fixed time budget, the CNN's extra cost per step can leave it far behind a simpler network, so judge learning per step as well as per minute. Read the learning curve before deciding a model is bad, because a curve still rising steeply means the run stopped too early.
result.prediction_check: The lesson predicted that the CNN would get fewer steps in 10 minutes; that held (about 103,000 against about 650,000 for the MLP), but the hope that it would learn more from the same view did not hold within this budget.

recommendations.title: Give the CNN 30 minutes
recommendations.why: The CNN's curve jumped from 1.08 to 10.36 apples in the last 5 minutes, so it may have been cut off before it levelled off. Testing a longer budget checks whether it catches the MLP given time.
recommendations.change: Raise the time budget from 10 to 30 minutes, keeping the CNN and every other setting the same.
recommendations.prediction: The CNN's test mean rises to between 20 and 30 apples, with about 300,000 env steps, still below the MLP's 31.6 at 10 minutes.
recommendations.question: Is the CNN still climbing, and does more time close the gap to the MLP?

recommendations.title: Shorten the CNN's exploration phase
recommendations.why: Exploration decays over 100,000 steps, about the whole length of this run, so the CNN may have spent most of its learning acting randomly. A shorter decay should let it exploit what it learns sooner.
recommendations.change: Lower eps_decay_steps for the CNN from 100,000 to 20,000, keeping the 10-minute budget.
recommendations.prediction: The test mean rises by at least 5 points, to about 18 or more apples, and the body-crash share stays near 100 percent.
recommendations.question: Is the CNN slow because it explores for too long, and not only because each step is expensive?

ideas.title: Compare algorithms at equal env steps
ideas.what: Add a dashboard view that plots the learning curve against env steps as well as wall-clock minutes, and reports the score each run reached at a chosen step count.
ideas.why: The CNN ran about 6 times slower per step, so comparing at equal minutes mixes up how fast it learns with how fast it computes; this run's lesson question is about learning per step.
ideas.expected: Shows whether the CNN is more sample-efficient than the MLP even though it is far behind at 10 minutes (for example, its score at about 100,000 env steps against the MLP's score at the same step count).
